findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Replacing the multiple-providers IllegalStateException with silent selection turns a previously-fatal classpath misconfiguration into silent misconfiguration tolerance; since DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order()==200, having two on the classpath yields a nondeterministic, silently-chosen provider based on ServiceLoader iteration order

[Medium/api] CryptoProvider.java:39 — Adding abstract order() to the public CryptoProvider interface without a default implementation breaks all external/third-party implementors at compile time on upgrade

[Medium/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:66 (getBouncyCastleProvider) — Returns the default KeyStore provider (e.g. SUN/SunJSSE) instead of BouncyCastle, giving callers a semantically wrong provider; it also constructs a full KeyStore instance just to fetch its provider

[Medium/bug] META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider:19 — Provider is registered globally via ServiceLoader but nearly all methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, so other keycloak-common consumers sharing the classpath (PEM parsing, JWE, cert validation via CryptoIntegration.getProvider()) fail at runtime with an opaque 'Not supported yet.' exception instead of getting a capable provider

[Medium/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:52 — Test only verifies a roundtrip (RS→DER→RS), so a symmetric bug in both conversion directions (e.g. consistent off-by-one or truncation) would pass; should assert DER output matches a known-good encoding and/or that a DER-converted signature still verifies

[Low/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:113-114 (concatenatedRSToASN1DER) — Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to but their output is discarded before the real encoding is built

[Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:60-70 (readSequence) — Indefinite-length encoding (readLength() returns -1) is not handled: the while (length > 0) loop is skipped and an empty list silently returned instead of an error; similarly readNext() computes a bogus length (-1 + header bytes) and misparses the stream

[Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:66-71 — readSequence never validates that elements exactly consume the sequence content; if an inner element exceeds the declared content length, length goes negative and the loop silently exits, accepting truncated/malformed input

[Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest / build config — No test exercises the actual integration path: CryptoIntegration.init + ServiceLoader discovery of AuthzClientCryptoProvider (e.g. a typo in the services file or an order() regression would not be caught), and no test covers AuthzClient.create() invoking crypto init

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider:19 — Provider is registered globally via ServiceLoader but nearly all methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, so other keycloak-common consumers sharing the classpath (PEM parsing, JWE, cert validation via CryptoIntegration.getProvider()) fail at runtime with an opaque 'Not supported yet.' exception instead of getting a capable provider

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new ServiceLoader registration `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` pointing to `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, but that implementation throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")` for most `CryptoProvider` methods (e.g., `getPemUtils`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getSignature`, ciphers, etc.). `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` now selects a provider (highest `order()`) instead of failing when multiple exist, and `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` explicitly calls `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())`, making it likely this provider will be used in authz-client-only classpaths. Any other keycloak-common code in the same app that calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider()` and then uses unsupported functionality would now fail at runtime with the opaque UOE, which is a concrete behavior risk introduced by the service registration plus partial implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:52 — Test only verifies a roundtrip (RS→DER→RS), so a symmetric bug in both conversion directions (e.g. consistent off-by-one or truncation) would pass; should assert DER output matches a known-good encoding and/or that a DER-converted signature still verifies

adjudication.rationale: In authz/client/src/test/java/.../ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java, the test signs data to get a DER ECDSA signature, converts DER→RS (asn1derToConcatenatedRS), then RS→DER (concatenatedRSToASN1DER), then DER→RS again and only asserts rsConcat equals rsConcat2. This roundtrip can pass even if both conversion methods share the same systematic error (e.g., incorrect padding/truncation) because the second conversion undoes the first. The test does not assert the produced DER matches the original DER signature nor that the converted DER signature still verifies, so the finding is a valid, diff-grounded test coverage concern rather than a concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:66-71 — readSequence never validates that elements exactly consume the sequence content; if an inner element exceeds the declared content length, length goes negative and the loop silently exits, accepting truncated/malformed input

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the loop subtracts each element’s total encoded length (returned by readNext()) from the declared sequence content length, but never checks for over-consumption. If an element’s encoded length exceeds the remaining declared length, `length` becomes negative and the `while (length > 0)` loop stops without throwing, returning a list that includes an element that could not fit within the declared sequence length. This is consistent with the finding and is verifiable from lines `while (length > 0) { ... length = length - bytes.length; }`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest / build config — No test exercises the actual integration path: CryptoIntegration.init + ServiceLoader discovery of AuthzClientCryptoProvider (e.g. a typo in the services file or an order() regression would not be caught), and no test covers AuthzClient.create() invoking crypto init

adjudication.rationale: The only added test (ECDSAAlgorithmTest) instantiates AuthzClientCryptoProvider directly and calls its ECDSA conversion methods; it does not exercise the new integration path where AuthzClient.create(Configuration) calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) and CryptoIntegration then discovers providers via ServiceLoader using the new META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider file and the new order()-based selection logic. Therefore, a broken services entry or provider ordering/regression would not be caught by tests in this diff.
